name: Ramp
text: Add a single, high-contrast focus ring that appears immediately on keyboard navigation. This ensures keyboard users can see where they are without extra clutter, meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA. The trade-off is a slight visual shift for mouse users, but it’s minimal and improves usability for everyone.

name: Reader
text: A single high-contrast ring risks creating a visual "siren" that pulls attention away from the task, especially for users with cognitive disabilities or ADHD. Instead, use a subtle but visible focus indicator that adapts to the user’s motion preferences—like reduced motion or touch-first—so it’s always present but never jarring. Settle it with user testing: if sighted keyboard users can’t track focus within 3 seconds, or if any participant reports distraction, the design fails.

name: Ramp
text:
Use a **subtle focus ring that respects motion preferences**: it appears immediately on keyboard navigation but fades out for users who prefer reduced motion. This balances visibility for keyboard users with cognitive comfort for others, meeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA without creating a distracting "siren" effect. The trade-off is slightly slower visual feedback for keyboard users who rely on the ring, but the adaptability ensures it doesn’t disrupt their workflow.

name: Reader
text: The proposed subtle focus ring still risks being insufficient for users with low vision or cognitive impairments, as it may not provide the strong visual cue needed to indicate focus. A better alternative is to implement a focus indicator that combines both subtlety and strength, perhaps using a color change alongside a slight glow effect. To settle the argument, testing with real users should determine if this solution effectively meets the needs of diverse users without being overwhelming.
